Rashi on Shevuot 4a:10:2.hebrew: ותו ה"ז בעולה ויורד - והא במזיד אוקימתה:
Rashi on Shevuot 4a:10:2.english: And furthermore, this one is [liable to bring] a sliding-scale offering - But you have established it as [dealing with] one who acted intentionally:

Rashi on Shevuot 4a:11:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רב יוסף - לעולם לקרבן, ודקשיא לך לא רבי ישמעאל ולא ר"ע היא — ר' סתמה, ואליבא דתנאי. וה"ג, בשבועות נסיב לה כר"ע, בידיעות נסיב לה כר' ישמעאל, ולא מסתם סתמינהו, אלא ה"ק: שבועות לר"ע שתים שהן ד', ידיעות לר' ישמעאל שתים שהן ד':
Rashi on Shevuot 4a:11:1.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said - Indeed, [the mishna refers] to a sacrifice; and as for what troubles you, that it is neither Rabbi Yishmael nor Rabbi Akiva — it is Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], who taught it anonymously and according to [different] tanna'im. And so here: with regard to oaths he formulated it according to Rabbi Akiva, and with regard to awareness [of defilement] he formulated it according to Rabbi Yishmael. And he did not teach them as a blanket anonymous ruling; rather, this is what it says: Oaths, according to Rabbi Akiva, are two that are four; awareness, according to Rabbi Yishmael, are two that are four.

Rashi on Shevuot 4a:12:1.hebrew: אמריתא לשמעתא כו' - אני פירשתי שמועה זו של רב יוסף לפני רב כהנא, ואמר לי דהאי נסיב לה אליבא דתנאי. דקאמר רב יוסף "לא תימא נסיב ולא ס"ל, ולא סתמינהו", אלא ודאי מסתם סתמינהו רבי, והכי קסבר לה: בשבועות כר"ע, ובידיעות כר' ישמעאל, וטעמא דנפשיה קאמר:
Rashi on Shevuot 4a:12:1.english: I said this statement, etc. - I explained this statement of Rav Yosef before Rav Kahana, and he said [to me] that this [Rabbi] formulates it according to [different] *tanna'im*. For Rav Yosef said, "Do not say that he formulates it [according to others] but does not hold [that way himself], and that he did not state them anonymously." Rather, certainly Rabbi stated them anonymously, and this is what he holds: regarding oaths, like Rabbi Akiva, and regarding the knowledge [of impurity], like Rabbi Yishmael; and he is stating his own reasoning.

Rashi on Shevuot 4a:13:1.hebrew: ונעלם ונעלם שני פעמים - תרי "ונעלם" כתיבי גבי טומאת קרבן עולה ויורד: "ונעלם ממנו והוא טמא" (ויקרא ה׳:ג׳), "ונעלם ממנו והוא ידע" (שם). קמא דוקא, למיגמר מיניה על העלם טומאה הוא חייב, ואינו חייב על העלם מקדש. ואידך קרא יתירא הוא, לדרשא הטל "והוא ידע" בין תרי "ונעלם", ודרוש דלאחר שהיתה ידיעה נעלם. ולמימר דבעי ידיעה בתחלה וידיעה בסוף, לא צריכא קרא, דאי לא ידע שחטא, אמאי לייתי קרבן:
Rashi on Shevuot 4a:13:1.english: "And it was concealed," "and it was concealed" twice - Two [instances of] "and it was concealed" are written with regard to impurity [in the context] of the sliding-scale offering: "And it was concealed from him, and he is impure" (Leviticus 5:2–3), "and it was concealed from him, and he knew" (ibid.). The first is specifically [to teach] that from it we learn that he is liable for a lapse of awareness of impurity, but he is not liable for a lapse of awareness of the Temple [i.e., that he entered it]. And the other verse is extra, [to be] expounded: place "and he knew" between the two [instances of] "and it was concealed," and expound that after there had been awareness, it was concealed. But to say that one requires awareness at the beginning and awareness at the end, no verse is needed, for if he did not know that he sinned, why would he bring an offering?

Rashi on Shevuot 4a:1:1.hebrew: אינו חייב אלא אחת - דמאחר שנשבע עליו שבועה ראשונה נאסרת עליו, וכי הדר אישתבע ה"ל נשבע לקיים את המצוה. ותנן לקמן (שבועות דף כז.): נשבע לקיים את המצוה ולא קיים, פטור משבועת קרבן:
Rashi on Shevuot 4a:1:1.english: He is liable only for one - For since he swore on it the first oath, it [the item] became forbidden to him, and when he swore again, it is [a case of] one who swore to fulfill a commandment. And we learned below (Shevuot 27a): One who swore to fulfill a commandment and did not fulfill it is exempt from the oath-offering:

Rashi on Shevuot 4a:1:2.hebrew: זו היא - להבא דלקי עלה, דהויא לה לאו שיש בו מעשה. אבל אם אמר אוכל ולא אכל, לא לקי:
Rashi on Shevuot 4a:1:2.english: This is - [an oath] regarding the future, for which one receives lashes, since it is a prohibition that involves an action. But [if one said] "I will eat" and did not eat, he does not receive lashes.

Rashi on Shevuot 4a:5:1.hebrew: אלא מעיקרא סבר לה כו' - הלכך רבי יוחנן ס"ל כסתמא בתרא, דהדר ביה רבי מקמייתא:
Rashi on Shevuot 4a:5:1.english: Rather, initially he held it, etc. - Therefore, Rabbi Yochanan holds [in accordance with] the later unattributed [mishna], for Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] retracted from the earlier one.

Rashi on Shevuot 4a:5:2.hebrew: ומשנה לא זזה ממקומה - ומשנה ראשונה, אע"פ שחזר בו מסתימתה, מאחר שפשטה ברוב התלמידים, לא היה יכולת בדורות שאחר רבי לשכחה מפיהם ולבטלה מבית המדרש, והניחו את שתיהן. והמשכיל יבין שאחרונה עיקר, שחזר בו מן הראשונה:
Rashi on Shevuot 4a:5:2.english: And a mishna does not move from its place - And the first mishna, even though he retracted from its unattributed [ruling], since it had spread among most of the students, the generations after Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] were unable to make it forgotten from their mouths and to remove it from the study hall, and they left both of them [in place]. And the discerning person will understand that the latter one is the main [ruling], for he retracted from the first.

Rashi on Shevuot 4a:7:1.hebrew: לאו שניתן לאזהרת מיתת ב"ד - לאו האמור בשבת לא ניתן לעונש מלקות, אלא שאם יעבור עליו, יתרה בו המתרה שהוא בסקילה, ויסקל. ואם לא התרה בו סקילה, והתרה בו מלקות, אין דינו ללקות, שלא לעונש מלקות כתבו מתחלה. ומשנינן: להכי אוקימנא כרבי ישמעאל, דאמר במסכת מכות: לאו שניתן לאזהרת מיתת ב"ד, אם התרו בו מלקות ולא מיתה, מלקין אותו. דתניא: אחת חייבי כריתות ואחת חייבי מיתות ב"ד ישנן בכלל מלקות מ', דברי רבי ישמעאל:
Rashi on Shevuot 4a:7:1.english: A prohibition that was given as a warning for [a transgression punishable by] court-imposed death - The prohibition stated regarding Shabbat was not given for the punishment of lashes; rather, if one transgresses it, the warner warns him that it is [punishable] by stoning, and he is stoned. But if he did not warn him of stoning, and warned him of lashes, he is not liable to be flogged, since [the Torah] did not write it originally for the punishment of lashes. And we answer: Therefore we established [the mishna] according to Rabbi Yishmael, who said in tractate Makkot: [For] a prohibition that was given as a warning for [a transgression punishable by] court-imposed death, if they warned him of lashes and not of death, we flog him. As it was taught: Both those liable to karet and those liable to court-imposed death are included in [the law of] the forty lashes; these are the words of Rabbi Yishmael.

Rashi on Shevuot 4a:8:1.hebrew: הא לאו הכי מתוקמא כר"ע - בתמיה: והא קשיא ידיעות הטומאה, כדאמר לעיל (שבועות דף ג.) דלר"ע אינו חייב על העלם קדש ומקדש:
Rashi on Shevuot 4a:8:1.english: Were it not for this, [the mishna] could be established in accordance with Rabbi Akiva - [This is stated] as a rhetorical question: But [surely] the [mishna's mention of] awareness of the impurity poses a difficulty, as stated above (Shevuot 3a), that according to Rabbi Akiva one is not liable for lapse of awareness of [the sanctity of] the Temple or its sacred foods.

Rashi on Shevuot 4a:8:2.hebrew: ומשני לאו אמרת ר' ישמעאל היא - דהוי קשיא לן שבועות גבי קרבן, ואוקימנא למלקות. ולא קשיא לן לר"ע נמי, אי לאו משום קושיא דלאו שניתן לאזהרת מיתת ב"ד, דשמעינן ליה לר"ע במס' מכות דאין לוקין עליו. אי הוה קשיא לן ידיעות לקרבן, הוה מוקמינן לה למלקות כולה מתניתין ור"ע, והוה ניחא לן לאוקמה אליבא דר"ע, משום דכולהו סתימתאי אליבי' דאמרי' (סנהדרין דף פו.) סתם מתני' ר"מ, סתם ספרא ר' יהודה, סתם תוספתא ר' נחמיה, וכולהו אליבא דר"ע ממנו קבלו:
Rashi on Shevuot 4a:8:2.english: And [the Gemara] answers: Didn't you say it is Rabbi Yishmael - For the [mention of] oaths alongside the offering was difficult for us, and we established it as referring to lashes. And it would not be difficult for us [to establish it] according to Rabbi Akiva as well, were it not for the difficulty of a prohibition that was given as a warning for a death penalty of the court, for we know from Rabbi Akiva in tractate Makkot that one is not flogged for it. [But] if the [mention of] awareness with regard to an offering were what was difficult for us, we would establish the whole mishna as referring to lashes, and [as per] Rabbi Akiva, and it would be well for us to establish it according to Rabbi Akiva, because all the anonymous [teachings] are in accordance with him, as we say (Sanhedrin 86a): An anonymous mishna is Rabbi Meir, an anonymous Sifra is Rabbi Yehuda, an anonymous Tosefta is Rabbi Nechemya, and all are in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, from whom they received [their traditions].

Rashi on Shevuot 4a:9:1.english: If so - that the mishna is [speaking] about lashes.

Rashi on Shevuot 4a:9:2.hebrew: ידיעות - דמשמע ונעלמו. היכי תנן? הא התראות נינהו, ואין כאן העלם:
Rashi on Shevuot 4a:9:2.english: Awarenesses - For it implies [the case of] "and it was hidden" [i.e., a lapse of awareness]. How [then] did we learn [it in the mishna]? These are [cases of] forewarnings, and there is no lapse of awareness here.

Rashi on Shevuot 4a:9:3.hebrew: הא לא קשיא - כלומר, אם אין לך קושיא אחרת, זו יש לתרץ כך:
Rashi on Shevuot 4a:9:3.english: This is not difficult - That is, if you have no other difficulty, this one can be resolved in this way.

Tosafot on Shevuot 4a:2:1.hebrew: אבל אוכל ולא אכל לא לקי - דלמעט "אכלתי ולא אכלתי" לא אתי, כדאמר בפ"ג (לקמן שבועות דף כא: ושם), דקאי בלהבא וממעט להבא, ולא אזרוק וזרק חייב לכ"ע. וליכא למימר נמי דאתי למעוטי נשבע לבטל המצוה, דהא קתני לה התם (דף כז.) ברישא דהך מתני'. וא"ת: היכי דייק מהכא דלאו שאין בו מעשה אין לוקין עליו? דלמא טעמא משום דהוי התראת ספק. וי"ל: דמשמע ליה דפטר אפילו נשבע על הככר וזרקו לים והתרו בו בשעת זריקה. ומיהו הא נמי חשיב התראת ספק למ"ד ביטלו ולא בטלו דחשיב התראת ספק, אפילו שיבר כנפיה, בפ' בתרא דמכות (דף טו: ושם). א"נ אינו חושש רק למצוא תנא דפליג אמתני'. וא"ת: ומנלן דפליג? דלמא מתני' דהכא איירי בזורק ככר לים דהוי התראת ודאי, ולעולם תרוייהו סבירא להו דלוקין על לאו שאין בו מעשה, ומתני' דפ"ג (לקמן שבועות דף כז:) איירי בהתראת ספק. וי"ל: דמתני' משמע ליה דאיירי כמתני' דלקמן (שם). וכן מייתי לעיל שפיר ממתני' דמותיר בטהור, אע"ג דאיכא למימר דפטר משום דיש בהן התראת ספק, דמ"מ אייתי ראיה דפליג תנא אמתני', דבהאי טעמא דפטר מותיר בטהור יש לפטור הך דמתניתין:
Tosafot on Shevuot 4a:2:1.english: But [if one says,] "I will eat," and did not eat, he is not flogged - [This is] because [the Mishnah's phrase] "to exclude" does not come to exclude [the case of] "I ate" and "I did not eat," as it says in chapter 3 (below, Shevuot 21b, and there), for [the oath] refers to the future and excludes [only oaths about] the future, and [in the case of] "I will not throw," and he threw, he is liable according to all. Nor can we say that it comes to exclude one who swears to nullify a commandment, for [the Mishnah] teaches that case there (27a) in the first clause of this Mishnah. And if you ask: How does [the Gemara] infer from here that a prohibition that involves no action is not punished with lashes? Perhaps the reason [for exemption] is that it constitutes a doubtful warning. And one can answer: [The Gemara] understands that [the Mishnah] exempts even one who swore about a loaf and threw it into the sea, and was warned at the time of the throwing. However, this too is considered a doubtful warning according to the one who says [that when] he nullified it, it was not [truly] nullified, which is considered a doubtful warning, even if he broke its wing, in the last chapter of Makkot (15b, and there). Alternatively, [the Gemara] is concerned only to find a Tanna who disagrees with the Mishnah. And if you ask: How do we know that he disagrees? Perhaps the Mishnah here deals with one who throws a loaf into the sea, which is a definite warning, and in truth both [Tannaim] hold that one is flogged for a prohibition that involves no action, and the Mishnah of chapter 3 (below, 27b) deals with a doubtful warning. And one can answer: [The Gemara] understands that the Mishnah deals [with a case] like the Mishnah below (there). And so, above, [the Gemara] properly brings [a proof] from the Mishnah of one who leaves over [the remains of an offering] from what is pure, even though one could say that [the Mishnah] exempts because there is a doubtful warning in them; in any case, [the Gemara] brought proof that a Tanna disagrees with the Mishnah, for by this reasoning that exempts [one who] leaves over from what is pure, one should exempt this [case] of our Mishnah:

Tosafot on Shevuot 4a:5:1.hebrew: והדר סבר לאו שאין בו מעשה אין לוקין עליו - וא"ת דבריש אלו טריפות (חולין דף מג.) פריך לר' יוחנן דאמר הלכה כדברי האומר בכזית: והא"ר יוחנן הלכה כסתם משנה, ותנן: ניטלה הכבד ולא נשתייר ממנה כלום! ומאי פריך? והא סתמא בתרא עדיף! וי"ל דאלו טריפות ואלו כשירות חדא מילתא היא, ולא שייך למימר בהו קמייתא ובתרייתא. והר"ר יעקב דאורלינ"ש תירץ דה"פ: והא"ר יוחנן הלכה כסתם משנה — ע"כ סתמא דאלו כשירות לאו סתמא מעלייתא היא, דאי סתם גמור הוא אמאי הוצרך לפסוק כוותיה? והא"ר יוחנן חדא זימנא דהלכה כסתם משנה:
Tosafot on Shevuot 4a:5:1.english: "And later he held that for a prohibition that does not involve an action, one is not flogged" - And if you ask: In the beginning of [the chapter] "These are the terefot" (Chullin 43a), [the Gemara] challenges Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said that the halakha follows the one who says [the measure is] an olive-bulk: But didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say that the halakha follows an unattributed mishna, and we learned [in an unattributed mishna]: "If the liver was removed and nothing of it remained [it is a *tereifa*]"! And what is the challenge? Isn't the later unattributed [mishna] preferable? And one can answer that "these are *terefot*" and "these are valid" are one matter, and it is not applicable to speak of them as an earlier and a later [mishna]. And Rabbeinu Yaakov of Orléans answered that this is what [the Gemara] means: But didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say that the halakha follows an unattributed mishna — [then] necessarily the unattributed [mishna] of "these are valid" is not a proper unattributed [mishna], for if it were a definitive unattributed [mishna], why was it necessary [for Rabbi Yoḥanan] to rule in accordance with it? But Rabbi Yoḥanan already said once that the halakha follows an unattributed mishna:

Tosafot on Shevuot 4a:6:1.hebrew: מראות נגעים מאי מלקות איכא - ואין לומר כגון אם התרו בו שלא ליכנס למקדש ונכנס, או שלא לאכול בשר קודש ואכל, דא"כ היינו ידיעות הטומאה. ואם התרו בו שלא ליכנס במחנה לויה ונכנס לפנים ממחיצתו, הא אמר בפרק אלו דברים (פסחים דף סז. וע"ש בתד"ה הכתוב) דלא לקי, שהכתוב נתקו לעשה, דכתיב "בדד ישב". אבל אי איירי לענין קרבן ניחא, דיש קרבן לאחר שנטהר מנגעו:
Tosafot on Shevuot 4a:6:1.english: Shades of leprous marks — what lashes are there? - One cannot say [that it refers to] a case where they warned him not to enter the Temple and he entered, or not to eat sacred meat and he ate, for then this would be [the case of] "awareness of impurity" [itself]. And if they warned him not to enter the Levite camp and he entered within its boundary — [the Gemara] already said in the chapter "Eilu Devarim" (Pesachim 67a, and see there in Tosafot, s.v. Hakatuv) that he does not receive lashes, because the verse severed it [from lashes by making it] a positive commandment, as it is written: "He shall dwell alone." But if [the Mishnah] is speaking with regard to a sacrifice, it is well, for there is a sacrifice after he is purified from his leprosy.

Tosafot on Shevuot 4a:6:2.hebrew: בקוצץ בהרתו - משמע הכא דאין לוקין אלא על קציצת ד' מראות נגעים. וקשה, דבפ' ר"א דמילה (שבת דף קלב: ושם) משמע דלקי אף על קציצת נגעים טהורים, דאין צרעת דוחה את העבודה, ופריך: ונקצץ בהרתו! דאתי עשה דעבודה ודחי לאו דקוצץ בהרתו, ומשני: מחוסר טבילה. התינח נגעים טמאים; נגעים טהורין מאי איכא למימר? משמע דלקי אקציצת נגעים טהורים. ואומר ריצב"א דהתם נמי לא איירי אלא בד' מראות, וטהורים דקאמר, כגון דעמד בעיניו בזה ובזה, או כהה, וקרי ליה טהורה לפי שאין מוחלט ואין מחוסר טבילה שכבר טבל:
Tosafot on Shevuot 4a:6:2.english: Where one cuts off his baheret - It implies here that one is liable to lashes only for cutting off the four shades of leprous marks. But this is difficult, for in the chapter [entitled] "Rabbi Eliezer [says, if one did not bring the implement the day before]" regarding circumcision (Shabbat 132b, there) it implies that one is lashed even for cutting off pure marks, for leprosy does not override the Temple service. And [the Gemara] asks: Let him cut off his baheret! [This works] because the positive commandment of the service comes and overrides the prohibition of cutting off one's baheret. And it answers: [He is] lacking immersion. This works [to explain] impure marks; but as for pure marks, what is there to say? This implies that one is lashed for cutting off pure marks. And the Rizva says that there too it speaks only of the four shades, and the "pure" ones it mentions are, for example, where [the mark] remained [unchanged] in his eyes in both this [week] and that, or it faded, and it calls it pure because he is not [a confirmed] leper and he is not lacking immersion, for he already immersed:

Tosafot on Shevuot 4a:8:1.hebrew: הא לאו הכי מתוקמא כר"ע קשה ידיעות - תימה: דהא ודאי אי הוה סבר ר"ע לאו שניתן לאזהרת מיתת ב"ד לוקין עליו, הוה אתיא מתני' שפיר כר"ע, ולא הוה קשיא ליה ידיעות, כיון דלמלקות איירי מתני'; דאיצטריך למימר דסבר תנא דמתניתין לאו שניתן לאזהרת מיתת ב"ד לוקין עליו? וי"ל: דקשיא ליה ידיעות כי מוקמינן מתני' כר"ע, אע"ג דמתניתין איירי למלקות, כדמסיק בתר הכי: אי הכי, ידיעות התראות מיבעי ליה. אבל כרבי ישמעאל ולמלקות אתי שפיר הא דקתני ידיעות, דמתני' איירי בין לקרבן בין למלקות. והשתא אתי שפיר דיש ליישב אי הכי דפריך, אמאי מוקי כרבי עקיבא ולמלקות, דכרבי ישמעאל ולמלקות א"ש כדפרישית:
Tosafot on Shevuot 4a:8:1.english: "Were it not for this, the mishna can be established in accordance with Rabbi Akiva — [then] 'awareness' poses a difficulty" - It is surprising: For certainly, if Rabbi Akiva held that one is flogged for a prohibition that is given as a warning for a [transgression punishable by] death by the court, the mishna would work out well according to Rabbi Akiva, and 'awareness' would not pose a difficulty for [the Gemara], since the mishna is speaking about lashes. [So] why was it necessary to say that the Tanna of the mishna holds that one is flogged for a prohibition that is given as a warning for [a transgression punishable by] death by the court? And one can answer: [The Gemara] finds 'awareness' difficult when we establish the mishna as [following] Rabbi Akiva, even though the mishna is speaking about lashes, as [the Gemara] concludes afterward: If so, it should have said 'warnings.' But according to Rabbi Yishmael and [the mishna being] about lashes, the term 'awareness' that [the mishna] teaches works out well, for the mishna is speaking both of an offering and of lashes. And now it works out well, for one can resolve [the Gemara's question] 'If so,' where it asks why [the Gemara] establishes [the mishna] as [following] Rabbi Akiva and about lashes — for according to Rabbi Yishmael and about lashes it works out well, as I explained:

Tosafot on Shevuot 4a:8:2.hebrew: רבי עקיבא נמי ולמלקות - וא"ת: א"כ סבר ר"ע לאו שאין בו מעשה לוקין עליו, כדאמר הגמ' לעיל אליבא דר' ישמעאל, והיכי מצי סבר דלוקין עליו? והא למ"ד לוקין עליו — משום דגמר ממוציא ש"ר ועדים זוממין, כדאמר בפ"ק דמכות (דף ב:), ור"ע דאומר עדים זוממין קנסא הוא — לא מצי גמר, דאיכא למימר: שכן קנס! וי"ל, דדלמא סבר כרב דימי דאמר בפ"ג (לקמן שבועות דף כ:): אכלתי ולא אכלתי — שבועת שוא היא, ולקי עליו מ"לא ינקה". ולמאי דפרישית לעיל דדוקא גבי שבועה קאמר לעיל דלקי עליו — אתי שפיר:
Tosafot on Shevuot 4a:8:2.english: Rabbi Akiva also [can hold that the mishna refers] to lashes - And if you ask: If so, Rabbi Akiva holds that one is flogged for a prohibition that involves no action, as the Gemara said above according to Rabbi Yishmael. But how can he hold that one is flogged for it? For according to the one who says that one is flogged for it, [this is] because he derives it from one who brings out a bad name, and from witnesses proven to be conspirators, as stated in the first chapter of Makkot (2b); but Rabbi Akiva, who says that [the punishment of] conspiring witnesses is a fine, cannot derive it, since one can say: [That is] because it is a fine! And one can answer: Perhaps he holds like Rav Dimi, who said in the third chapter (below, Shevuot 20b): "I ate" and "I did not eat" is a vain oath, and one is flogged for it [as derived from] "He shall not be cleared." And according to what I explained above, that it said above that one is flogged for it specifically with regard to an oath, it works out well:
